stories.title: “bonsoir, Elliot”: How abliterated models can get you pwned
stories.reason: ProjectDiscovery shows abliterated/edited open-weight models can carry an undetectable LoRA backdoor (~43M params, ~0.6% of base) that fires a malicious tool call on a trigger phrase; working PoC exfiltrated .env secrets from OpenAI Codex CLI for under $50 and 2.5 GPU-hours.
key_facts: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct backdoored via LoRA; triggered run exfiltrated dummy creds through Codex CLI
7B model: 20% poison rate -> 100% trigger fire rate, 100% clean-task accuracy
1.5B model: 1% poison -> 75-98% fire rate across seeds; 5% poison -> 99-100%
Total cost under $50; ~2.5 hours on one rented L4 GPU (~$8)
Cites Anthropic-style finding that ~250 poisoned documents can backdoor 600M-13B models
Protect AI scan found ~352,000 unsafe/suspicious files across 51,700 HF models
Standard benchmarks/scanners miss the backdoor; recommends sandboxing network vs exec, logging boundaries

stories.title: Fake Web3 Accelerator Uses npm Packages to Spread Malware and Hijack AI Agent Traffic
stories.reason: Elastic's REF8801: a fake Web3 'Apex Accelerator' lures crypto devs with free Claude/Gemini credits to run npm packages that install infostealers and also register an attacker-controlled MCP server in the victim's agent config, exposing prompts/tool outputs and letting the attacker inject instructions into the agent.
key_facts: Tracked as REF8801 by Elastic Security Labs; Russian-language commit comments found
npm packages (@apexacc/cli, @apexacc/audit, etc.) deliver fake 'due diligence' audits with fabricated findings
Windows chain: PowerShell -> PyInstaller -> UAC bypass -> Go stealer that patches AMSI/ETW, unhooks ntdll, exfils via Telegram
macOS chain: bash script drops CloudSyncD backdoor, phishes sudo password via fake auth prompt
Can intercept/redirect OpenRouter LLM requests and register a rogue MCP server to read prompts/history/tool output and inject instructions

stories.title: A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents
stories.reason: A hacker reportedly breached John Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins using a large fleet of AI agents; concrete AI-x-cyber breach of major industrial/consumer brands, but source site blocked fetch so details are from title/HN only.
key_facts: Title names John Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins as victims
HN thread (59 pts) had no technical discussion; Reuters coverage exists but was not fetchable

stories.title: The US orders every civilian agency to rip out DeepSeek, even tools built on it
stories.reason: DHS Order 2026-01 (signed July 24, 2026, public this week) bans DeepSeek and DeepSeek-derived third-party products across all federal civilian agencies, with a 60-day exception window; major AI policy story with real enforcement teeth.
key_facts: DHS Order 2026-01, Secretary Markwayne Mullin, issued under 2018 supply-chain law
Covers DeepSeek plus third-party products/services built on DeepSeek implementations
Excludes national-security systems (Pentagon/DNI); civilian agencies must remove DeepSeek immediately
60-day window for written exception requests; CISA reviews; annual re-review required
Cites Feb 2025 NowSecure iOS audit and Apr 2025 House Select Committee report as evidence
Federal Register publication scheduled Oct 20, 2026, docket DHS-2026-0628

stories.title: HardEval: An Execution-Verified Benchmark for AI-Driven Security Hardening and Compliance Remediation
stories.reason: HardEval is a new, code-released benchmark that grades LLMs on actually hardening a live RHEL8 system against STIG controls (via OpenSCAP/OVAL pass/fail), not just writing plausible-looking fix scripts; tests 14 frontier/open models and finds large, uneven gaps by security domain.
key_facts: Grades via OpenSCAP/OVAL compliance check on a live VM, not static code review
Covers SSH config, authentication policy, audit rules, kernel parameters
Common failure mode: plausible code that doesn't satisfy the exact compliance condition
Evaluated 14 frontier and open-weight model configurations
Code/data released at github.com/manoharvellala/Hardeval

stories.title: Harness2 by Google Research – Recursive Agent Harnessing
stories.reason: Google Research's Harness2 keeps model weights fixed and instead recursively rewrites the agent harness itself (prompts, tools, memory, skills) using evidence from probe runs, reporting up to +11.8pp on one benchmark; real runnable code (Apache-2.0), not just a paper.
key_facts: Edits 8 harness components: system prompt, guardrails, memory, tool guidance, subagents, skills, scripts, plugins
Task-level recursion uses no ground-truth feedback; persistent 'improvement harness' carries lessons across tasks
Reported gains: up to 11.5 pts (WorkBuddy-Bench), 4.5 pts (JobBench), 11.8pp partial-pass (LAB) for GLM-5/Gemini 3.5 Flash
Local demo runs real Python with deterministic editors, no model credentials needed; benchmark runs need OpenCode/Codex executors
Apache 2.0, explicitly 'not an officially supported Google product'

stories.title: Mercury 3: Diffusion at scale
stories.reason: Inception's Mercury 3, billed as the most capable diffusion LLM yet, claims 1,068 tok/s (4-8x faster than comparable models) and parity with GPT-6 Luna / Claude Haiku 5.5 on benchmarks; big HN traction (226 pts) and the first real evidence diffusion LLMs scale like autoregressive ones.
key_facts: 1,068 tokens/sec on NVIDIA GPUs; 1M-token context (up from 260K in Mercury 2.5)
40x more parameters than Mercury 1; claims 3x benchmark intelligence gain over Mercury 1 mini
50% completion on 50 live Mind2Web browser-agent tasks, beating GPT-6.1-Sol per vendor
$0.20/$0.70 per M input/output tokens; available via API, OpenRouter, Baseten, Vercel
Vendor claims autoregressive scaling laws also hold for diffusion LLMs

stories.title: F5 releases out-of-band patches for critical NGINX vulnerabilities
stories.reason: F5 shipped out-of-band patches for three critical, unauthenticated NGINX flaws (DoS/RCE on non-default configs) across NGINX Plus/OSS/Ingress/Gateway Fabric/Instance Manager; no AI angle but NGINX's footprint and F5's recent record of being targeted make this a large pure-cyber headline.
key_facts: CVE-2026-15176 and CVE-2026-97205 in ngx_http_v3_module; CVE-2026-93479 in the map directive
Heap overflow / use-after-free in worker process; RCE possible if ASLR is off/bypassed
Not yet seen exploited in the wild per F5; CISA has listed 8 F5 CVEs as actively exploited since Nov 2021
Workarounds given for delayed patching (avoid alias/$request_filename, disable AIO/SSI, use named captures)
